Plan a path between two configurations

Source: R/planning.R
robot_plan.Rd

Runs the configured planner from start to goal. Start and goal are validated first. Randomness is reproducible: with seed the global random number state is restored afterwards and the seed is recorded in the result. A failure (success = FALSE) only means that no path was found within the iteration budget; it does not prove that no path exists. A successful path is collision-free only up to the discrete edge-checking resolution; verify it with robot_check_path(..., method = "continuous") when that matters.

Usage

robot_plan(planner, start, goal, seed = NULL, smooth = FALSE)

Arguments

planner

A robot_planner.

start, goal

Configurations.

seed

Optional integer seed.

smooth

Apply robot_shortcut() to a successful path.

Value

A robot_plan with path (one waypoint per row, or NULL), success, message, algorithm, iterations, nodes, length, seed and time (elapsed seconds).

Examples

planner <- robot_planner(validity = function(q) abs(q[1] - 0.5) > 0.1 || q[2] > 0.8,
                         bounds = rbind(c(0, 1), c(0, 1)))
plan <- robot_plan(planner, c(0.1, 0.1), c(0.9, 0.1), seed = 2)
plan
#> <robot_plan> rrt_connect: success
#> path found 
#> 11 waypoints, length 2.315, 37 nodes, 81 iterations, 0.012 s
#> seed: 2
